source.title: Training Feedforward Neural Networks with Standard Logistic Activations is Feasible
source.authors: Emanuele Sansone; F. D. De Natale

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no material truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests initialization effects on training outcomes in deep sigmoid networks, a conceptual test of V4's initialization and trainability claims, using MNIST rather than CIFAR and reporting training curves and test error rather than the exact measures in the versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own MNIST training-error results and initialization comparisons. The XOR and recurrent-task results do not directly measure the classification training-error behavior named by the versions and are not included. Referenced studies' results are not extracted as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The paper directly compares initialization strategies using training-objective learning curves in plain logistic networks. These results test V4's training-speed component. The extracted rows contain only test error and cannot establish that component.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors conclude that information-theoretically motivated initialization makes standard-logistic feedforward networks train successfully, with faster convergence and competitive generalization in their experiments. Their theoretical discussion explicitly does not guarantee freedom from vanishing gradients throughout training.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares initialization methods for standard-logistic networks on MNIST, not the versions' CIFAR classification-error recipes; its main intervention is information-theoretic initialization with elliptical projection.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization method changes convergence behavior and reported test error; data augmentation changes the MNIST test-error results.

fits_no_version.finding: Six-layer logistic MNIST test errors vary across initialization methods: 1.85–3.32% without augmentation and 0.68–0.82% with augmentation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization can affect final generalization performance in standard-logistic networks; test error alone does not identify training speed or trainable depth.

record.problems: The reported deep-network tables give test error, not training classification error; the experiment is on MNIST rather than CIFAR. Results are averaged over 4 random initializations, but the paper does not state a control for the claimed benchmark behavior.
record.rows_left_out: XOR shallow-network training curves and recurrent copy-memory and language-modeling results are outside the classification training-error behavior named in the versions. No rows from those sections were extracted.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, zero or near-zero training classification error, corrupted/random labels, and model-size or stopping effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks, and normalization-free residual training.

Maximum trainable depth is not measured by a depth sweep. The paper does not test very deep tanh networks, orthogonal versus equal-variance Gaussian weights in those networks, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks. Activation statistics provide indirect evidence about propagation; gradient preservation throughout training is not directly measured.
Learning rates relative to the initial stability limit, catapult recovery, curvature trajectories, edge-of-stability behavior and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Training-objective convergence comparisons for all six initializations in the shallow 800-unit MNIST network. Record the reported faster convergence separately from test error; equal total-run times in Table 1 are not times to a common loss target.

Training-objective convergence comparisons for the six-layer MNIST network. The text reports faster convergence with EP and slow early learning for competitors; these are the direct optimization results absent from R1–R6.
Training-objective convergence comparisons with data augmentation. The text reports that the convergence advantage persists; R7–R12 contain only final test errors.

Layerwise activation mean and standard-deviation trajectories: the text reports last-hidden-layer bias and little output variation for several comparators, with the unaugmented problem not visible for LSUV or EP. Record these as activation-propagation evidence, without treating them as direct gradient measurements.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. The extraction incorrectly treats V4 as requiring CIFAR training classification error; its training-speed component also applies to the reported logistic-network experiments. XOR and recurrent-task results were explicitly declared omitted, so they are not listed as missing. Numerical curve values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text; the verdicts use the authors' explicit descriptions.

versions.untested_parts: No CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or comparison of model size and early stopping is reported; MNIST results do not test this version's stated benchmark conditions.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or spurious-local-minimum frequency comparison.
No plain-versus-residual shortcut comparison, ImageNet or CIFAR-10 depth study, or normalization removal experiment.

Tests standard logistic initialization strategies and depth on MNIST, including orthogonal and the paper's proposed initialization. Does not test the cited activation-matched initializations across the full claimed settings, 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks, or very deep tanh networks.
No above-stability learning-rate experiment or sharpness measurement.

relationships.condition: Plain six-layer standard-logistic MNIST networks, with and without data augmentation
relationships.reason: Based on text and missing training-curve rows: Section 6.3 and Figures 5b–c report faster convergence with activation-specific EP initialization; LeCun, Glorot and orthogonal comparators learn slowly initially. R1–R12 record only test errors and do not supply this evidence.
relationships.display_finding: EP initialization accelerated convergence, while LeCun, Glorot and orthogonal initializations learned slowly initially.

relationships.condition: One-hidden-layer standard-logistic MNIST network with 800 hidden units
relationships.reason: Based on text and missing training-curve rows: Section 6.2 and Figure 5a report faster training-objective convergence with the proposed initialization despite similar final generalization across methods.
relationships.display_finding: The proposed initialization accelerated training-objective convergence despite similar final generalization across methods.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: MNIST deep sigmoid networks, with and without data augmentation
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports faster convergence for its proposed initializations and lower test error for them than several alternatives in the deep MNIST experiments (R5–R6, R11–R12); test error is only an indirect indicator of the version's trainability claim.
